facts.content: Patient reports lower abdominal ache and nausea for 2 days.
facts.source_text: CC: Lower abdominal ache and nausea x2 days

facts.content: Patient reports feeling subjectively febrile with sensations of being hot and sweaty.
Patient describes a dull, constant ache below the umbilicus.
facts.source_text: Abdomen: Dull, constant ache below umbilicus

facts.content: The lower abdominal ache worsens the patient's nausea.
The patient has nausea without vomiting.
The patient had constipation about one week ago which has resolved.
The patient's last bowel movement was yesterday.
The patient reports increased urinary frequency.
The patient denies pain on urination.
The patient denies urinary urgency.
The patient denies foul-smelling urine.
The patient denies vaginal discharge.
The patient has noted spotting or pink-coloured urine for the past few days.
facts.source_text: Vaginal/menstrual: Spotting/pink-coloured urine noted past few days

facts.content: The patient's last menstrual period was approximately more than 3 weeks ago and she is expecting menses soon.
facts.source_text: LMP ~3+ weeks ago; expecting menses soon

facts.content: The patient is sexually active with one partner.
The patient has an Implanon contraceptive implant in situ.
No past medical or surgical history is documented.
No medications are documented aside from the contraceptive implant.
Patient is allergic to amoxicillin.
The patient's brother has type 1 diabetes mellitus.
The patient lives with her boyfriend.
The patient is a non-smoker.
Lower abdominal pain with nausea for 2 days is assessed as probable benign or functional, possibly related to recent constipation, but remains undifferentiated abdominal pain requiring examination.
facts.source_text: 1. Lower abdominal pain with nausea x2 days — probable benign/functional causes (history of recent constipation) but undifferentiated abdominal pain requiring exam.

facts.content: Increased urinary frequency without dysuria is considered a urinary symptom of unclear etiology.
facts.source_text: 2. Increased urinary frequency without dysuria — urinary symptom of unclear etiology.

facts.content: Spotting or pink discoloration of urine around expected menses requires differentiation between hematuria and menstrual spotting.
facts.source_text: 3. Spotting/pink discoloration of urine around expected menses — need to differentiate hematuria vs menstrual spotting.

facts.content: Pregnancy needs to be excluded given sexual activity despite Implanon use.
facts.source_text: 4. Need to exclude pregnancy given sexual activity despite Implanon.

facts.content: Arrange same-day face-to-face GP review for abdominal and pelvic physical examination.
facts.source_text: Arrange same-day face-to-face GP review for physical exam (abdominal and pelvic)

facts.content: Perform a urine pregnancy test at the visit.
facts.source_text: Perform urine pregnancy test at visit

facts.content: Obtain a urine dip and send urine MSU for culture and sensitivity if indicated.
facts.source_text: Obtain urine dip (and send urine MSU/C&S if indicated)

facts.content: Order further blood tests and imaging as directed by the face-to-face clinician based on examination findings.
facts.source_text: Further bloods/imaging as directed by face-to-face clinician based on exam findings

facts.content: Safety-net advice given to seek urgent care or GP review sooner if symptoms worsen or if lightheadedness, presyncope, syncope, progressive fever, severe pain, vomiting, or new concerning symptoms develop.
facts.source_text: Safety-net: seek urgent care/GP sooner if symptoms worsen, develop lightheadedness, presyncope, syncope, fever progression, severe pain, vomiting, or new concerning symptoms
